 Deadline: Oct 25, 2026 @ 5:00pm MSK

 Overview 
 My projects 
 Participants (568) 
 Rules 
 Project gallery 
 Updates 
 Discussions 
 DATES 
  Learning and Training Sessions  
 • Session 1:  August 18, 2026 – Introducing IEEE Global ClimateChain Hackhaton Project 
 • Session 2: September 8, 2026 – AI and Cyber Security Issues for Climate Change 
 • Session 3: September 15, 2026 – Blockchain and AI for Climate Change 
 • Session 4: September 22, 2026 – Ethics and Responsibility for ClimateChain and Climate Change 
 • Session 5: October 5, 2026 – Good Practices for Climate Change 
 Eligibility
 Open Categories: 
 •       ✅ Students (undergraduate, graduate, PhD)
 •       ✅ Academic researchers and faculty
 •       ✅ Independent developers and startups
 •       ✅ Environmental professionals and climate scientists
 •       ✅ International participants (with country restrictions noted)
 Team Structure: 
 •       Teams of 2-5 members (individual submissions allowed)
 •       Cross-institutional and international collaboration encouraged.
 •       One person can only be on one team.
 Restrictions: 
 ❌ Hackathon organizers and immediate family (can mentor only)
   ❌ Judges and their immediate family
 ❌ Previous grand prize winners (can participate   for smaller awards)
 Project and Submission Requirements
 Track Alignment :  Clearly present the track you've chosen and explain how your project addresses the theme or challenge within that track.
 Demo Video (3–5 mins):  Showcase your project in action with a brief, focused demo video highlighting key features and functionality.
 Code Repository :  Include a link to your GitHub repo (or equivalent) that contains the source code and any relevant documentation.
 Deadline :  Make sure to submit your project before the official deadline to be considered for judging. Dont submit before official start time which 8 AM PT on October 25.
 Prizes TBD
 Judging Criteria and Winner Selection
 🌍 Climate Impact 
 How effectively does the project address a real climate or environmental challenge ? Does the solution contribute to improving sustainability, environmental transparency, carbon tracking, renewable energy adoption, or ecosystem protection?
 ✨ Innovation & Creativity 
 Is the idea fresh, innovative, and exciting ? Does it take a unique approach to applying blockchain or emerging technologies to solve climate-related challenges within the chosen track?
 🛠️ Technical Execution 
 Does the project function as intended ? Is the technology behind it well-implemented, technically sound, and appropriate for the proposed solution? Does it demonstrate effective use of tools such as blockchain, smart contracts, AI, data platforms, or environmental data integration ?
 📈 Practical Usefulness 
 How practical and scalable is the solution? Could the project realistically be used by organizations, communities, policymakers, or businesses to improve climate action, sustainability, or environmental monitoring?
 🎥 Presentation & Storytelling 
 Is the demo clear, engaging, and easy to understand ? Does the presentation effectively communicate:
 the climate problem being addressed
 how the solution works
 the potential real-world environmental impact
